A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 14-page D²R-UHDNet paper, including four supplementary pages. Text comparison and page rendering establish identical content except for the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original UHD restoration experiments in Tables 1–5, component ablations in Tables 6–8, and supplementary six-degradation results in Table 10.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original restoration experiments, ablations, quantitative results and supplementary visual comparisons.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and 9 retain identical D²R-UHDNet components, including CD²-VAE, Hi-CDL, OrthoGate, CIMF-Net and LaReNet, together with the same three-stage training procedure and losses.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same datasets and cover low-light enhancement, dehazing, deblurring, demoiréing, denoising, deraining and desnowing. The four- and six-degradation all-in-one scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in corresponding Tables 1–5 and 10 and the visual comparisons, including DreamUHD, UHDformer, UHDDIP and the same task-specific and all-in-one baselines.

E3.justification: The dataset splits in Table 9, noise levels, evaluation metrics, training settings and full-size inference conditions are unchanged. Both retain 256×256 FLOP measurement and 4K runtime evaluation on an RTX 3090.

E4.justification: Section 5 retains the same component and backbone ablations in Tables 6–8 and feature/spectral analyses in Figures 5–6. Supplementary qualitative comparisons in Figures 7–10 are also identical.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged throughout both PDFs. The same numerical tables present point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative examples are identical. For example, Table 3 retains 29.84 dB PSNR and 0.861 SSIM for the proposed method, while supplementary Table 10 retains 28.11 dB average PSNR.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 and Algorithm 1 are unchanged, including the Stiefel constraint, orthogonal updates, complex invertibility formulation and training objectives. No mathematical argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about controlled information loss, feature disentanglement, efficient reconstruction and state-of-the-art results across six UHD restoration tasks with approximately 1M parameters.

C2.justification: Interpretations of Hi-CDL/OrthoGate complementarity, invertible fusion, information preservation and all-in-one applicability are identical. No limitation, failure condition or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: Sections 4.1 and 9 retain the same hardware, layer/module counts, learning-rate schedules, batch sizes, crop sizes and parameter-freezing instructions. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 44 numbered reference entries are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to DreamUHD, UHDformer, UHDDIP and other prior work.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 17 Mar 2025 to v2 dated 26 Jun 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology, section order and supplementary structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp is slightly repositioned. All other rendered content is identical, including Figures 1–10, Tables 1–10 and the supplementary page layouts.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the same method, claims, experimental evidence, mathematical content and reproducibility details, including the supplement. The version/date stamp update and its slight repositioning do not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's quality.
